newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures erode to lower close.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures erode to lower close.

text.p: IMM currency futures eroded morning gains, with most units ending moderately lower.
Traders pinned much of the afternoon's pressure on one result of the two-day summit of European Union leaders that began Friday in Dublin.

The EU leaders firmed up a budget pact that will exempt from fines countries that run a fiscal deficit of more than three percent of gross domestic product if their economies have fallen by two percent or more.
They said EU ministers would decide on fines for countries where GDP fell between 0.75 percent and two percent.
Traders and analysts viewed the pact as a compromise by Germany, which previously had espoused a hard-line approach to EU economic and budgetary membership requirements.
"The Germans capitulated," one foreign exchange economist concluded. "It's good for the dollar, bad for the mark."
Traders said the mark could continue under some pressure vis-a-vis the dollar near-term, although the mark might fare better against some other European currencies, especially the Swiss franc.
The Swiss unit was expected to continue lower technically and on ideas that Swiss rates are likely to stay low.
The Swiss unit dropped despite remarks by Swiss National Bank board member Bruno Gehrig. He said Swiss franc no long was clearly overvalued but was "justifiably valued."

Currencies tracked moves in U.S. debt and equity markets, which recovered as the day progressed and gradually weighed down futures, traders added. They also noted talk that hedge funds were selling yen and Swiss francs for dollars.

March yen fell $0.000045 to $0.008893, marks lost $0.0047 to $0.6472, Swiss franc fell $0.0055 to $0.7622, sterling lost $0.0006 to $1.6526, Can dollar fell $0.0027 to $0.7384, Aussie dollar off $.0007 to $0.7910, Mex peso up $0.000550 at $0.120300.
